jobs.title: Project Manager, Accellacare
jobs.description:
Project Manager, Accellacare - United Kingdom (Homebased)

ICON is a global healthcare intelligence and clinical research organisation united by a mission to bring new medicines and treatments to patients faster.

As a values-driven organisation, integrity, collaboration, agility, and inclusion are at the heart of how we work and interact with each other, customers, patients and suppliers.

This role is with Accellacare, part of ICON's clinical research network, where you’ll play a key role in transforming the clinical trial experience for patients and sponsors alike. Our global site network is designed with one goal in mind: to deliver better access, greater efficiency, and improved outcomes in clinical research.

We have an incredible opportunity for a Project Manager
to join ICON’s Accellacare
team. The Project Manager is responsible for the overall direction, coordination, implementation, execution, control and completion of single service global projects within the Accellacare network, ensuring consistency with ICON SOPs, study contracts, and budgets.

Location:
United Kingdom (Homebased)

What You Will Be Doing

Lead and manage the planning, execution, and monitoring of single service projects within the Accellacare program, ensuring adherence to project timelines, budgets, and quality standards
Define project scope, goals, deliverables, and resource requirements
Develop detailed project plans, timelines, and risk mitigation strategies
Assemble, coordinate, and support project teams to ensure successful delivery
Monitor project progress, quality, and budget using appropriate tools
Communicate regularly with stakeholders through progress reports and updates, and collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify and address project risks and issues
Manage project changes, conduct evaluations, and assess final outcomes

Your Profile

Must have experience at a clinical research site as a site support coordinator, site activation, site partner, project support coordinator
Must have previous experience with clinical trials project management
Must have previous experience with clinical trials timeline and budget management
Assertive and confident in communication, with the ability to lead discussions, set clear expectations, and address issues directly - face to face site negotiation
Time management skills with the ability to prioritize efficiently
Proactive mindset with strong critical thinking abilities to identify issues early and make sound, data-driven decisions
Detail-oriented with a focus on accuracy, thoroughness, and consistency
Must have Fluent English Communication, Writing and Reading
Bachelor’s degree, preferably in life sciences

What ICON Can Offer You

Our success depends on the quality of our people. That’s why we’ve made it a priority to build a diverse culture that rewards high performance and nurtures talent.

In addition to your competitive salary, ICON offers a range of additional benefits. Our benefits are designed to be competitive within each country and are focused on well-being and work life balance opportunities for you and your family.

Our Benefits Examples Include

Various annual leave entitlements
A range of health insurance offerings to suit you and your family’s needs.
Competitive retirement planning offerings to maximize savings and plan with confidence for the years ahead.
Global Employee Assistance Programme, LifeWorks, offering 24-hour access to a global network of over 80,000 independent specialized professionals who are there to support you and your family’s well-being.
Life assurance
Flexible country-specific optional benefits, including childcare vouchers, bike purchase schemes, discounted gym memberships, subsidized travel passes, health assessments, among others.

Visit our careers site to read more about the benefits ICON offers.

At ICON, inclusion & belonging are fundamental to our culture and values. We’re dedicated to providing an inclusive and accessible environment for all candidates. ICON is committed to providing a workplace free of discrimination and harassment. All qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager - Prestige Beauty Agency, Fully Remote
jobs.description:
**
PLEASE NOTE - THIS ROLE REQUIRES CLICKUP EXPERTISE.**

LOCATION

Fully remote. Must be based in the states of New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Illinois, Florida, or California.

ABOUT OGAKI

OGAKI is the social-first agency specializing in social media and influencer marketing for prestige beauty brands such as Laura Mercier, bareMinerals, Sulwhasoo, EltaMD, and Dr. Diamond's Metacine. We have been named the best social media + influencer agency by BeautyMatter, digital agency of the year by PR Net, and one of the top boutique agencies in the US by Business Insider.

As we scale into 2027, we're looking for a Senior Project Manager to run our operations from day one: someone who takes ownership of active projects and makes our systems better as they go.

THE ROLE

This is a primarily internal-facing role: you’ll independently run multiple concurrent beauty brand projects and own the operational engine that keeps strategists and creatives in sync with the account team. You’ll step into live projects in your first week, with onboarding from our fractional Head of Operations, and run them without day-to-day oversight.

We’ve built strong operational infrastructure, including ClickUp, workflow frameworks, and custom AI tools. You’ll partner with our fractional Head of Operations, who leads tool and AI builds; you own day-to-day operations and process. That means taking full ownership of these systems, pressure-testing them, and bringing us clear recommendations on what to keep, cut, and improve.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Operations & Systems (40%)

•     Own ClickUp as the single source of truth from day one: maintain boards, build filtered views and dashboards, set up automations, and enforce updates across the team
•     Audit our existing workflows, project charters, and documentation, then recommend and implement improvements
•     Lead weekly status meetings with the leadership team (15-minute pattern-spotting check-ins)
•     Act as the "living playbook": the go-to reference when the team asks "how do we handle X?"
•     Keep documentation in Google Drive current, and retire or rebuild processes that no longer serve the team
•     Train new team members and freelancers on our systems and tools
•     Identify where AI tools can speed up briefing, documentation, and reporting, and roll them out with the team (custom builds are handled by our Head of Operations).

Cross-Functional Delivery (40%)

•     Independently manage 5+ beauty brand projects with overlapping timelines
•     Coordinate 8+ team members, including designers, video editors, content creators, strategists, and copywriters
•     Translate client feedback and strategist concepts into clear, actionable creative briefs
•     Run seamless handoffs between strategy, creative, and social teams
•     Assess and manage change requests end to end: evaluate scope, timeline, and strategic fit, make the call, and escalate only when a decision is truly strategic or affects budget
•     Own deadlines across all projects, keeping the internal team informed on status and risks
•     Serve as a trusted day-to-day partner to the account team

Capacity & Resource Management (20%)

•     Partner with the Head of Social on team bandwidth across all active projects
•     Match specialists to projects based on skills, capacity, and client requirements
•     Flag capacity constraints early and propose solutions before they become missed deadlines
•     Maintain real-time clarity on who's working on what, when, and what's coming next

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

After 30 Days

•     You're running active client projects independently
•     You've met every team member and know who owns what
•     You've audited our ClickUp setup, workflows, and documentation
•     You've presented leadership with an initial set of process optimization recommendations, prioritized by impact

After 60 Days

•     You're leading weekly status meetings with leadership
•     You've implemented your first process improvements
•     Creatives report feeling well-briefed and clear on deliverables
•     Deadlines are consistently being met across the team
•     ClickUp is consistently current, and the team relies on it without reminders

After 90 Days

•     You're making confident calls on change requests, escalating only when truly strategic
•     Leadership sees measurable improvement in communication clarity, handoff smoothness, and deadline visibility
•     You're anticipating capacity and timeline problems before they reach leadership

After 6 Months

•     You've implemented at least 3 meaningful process improvements
•     The team proactively references your ClickUp boards and documentation
•     Systems are evolving based on your insights, not just being maintained

After 1 Year

•     You're the operational authority: the team comes to you first for process questions
•     The account team trusts you as the "make it happen" partner

MUST-HAVE QUALIFICATIONS

Experience

•     8+ years in project or program management, with at least 3 years at a social media, digital, or creative agency
•     Proven track record independently running 5+ concurrent client projects with minimal oversight
•     Experience coordinating cross-functional creative teams (designers, video editors, copywriters, creators) across multiple specialties at once
•     Demonstrated history of auditing and improving operational processes, with examples you can walk us through
•     Beauty, fashion, or lifestyle brand experience strongly preferred (we'll consider CPG or DTC e-commerce)
•     Success keeping distributed, remote teams aligned

Technical Competencies

•       Advanced ClickUp expertise required
: 2+ years hands-on experience building and administering workspaces, including custom views, dashboards, automations, and templates
•     Deep knowledge of social content production workflows
•     Google Workspace fluency: Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Calendar for organizational systems
•     Exceptional written communication: Slack messages and emails that are clear, concise, and actionable
•     Hands-on experience using AI tools for documentation, briefing, or workflow support

Nice to Have

•     PMP, Scrum, or similar certification

WHAT WE OFFER

Compensation & Benefits

•     Salary: $100k–$130k/year, commensurate with experience
•     Medical, vision, and dental insurance
•     401(k)
•     Summer Fridays
•     Generous PTO program

Work Environment

•     Fully remote: based in New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Illinois, or California
•     Modern tools: ClickUp, Google Workspace, Slack, and AI-powered operational tools
•     Real influence: your recommendations shape how OGAKI operates as we scale
•     Collaborative culture: you'll know everyone personally while working with prestige beauty brands
•     No corporate bureaucracy: direct access to the Founder and fast decision-making

jobs.description:

to join our Information Technology
team. If you’re looking for a company that embraces the principles of respect, compassion and trust, please apply with us today!

IT Project Manager

Location:
Can work remotely in the domestic United States
Schedule:
Regular business hours are 8:00am to 5:00pm Monday through Friday, must be able to work after hours and on weekends as needed.

WHAT YOU MUST POSSESS

Demonstrated experience with implementations and data transfers
Creative problem resolution skills. Excellent project management skills. Good quantitative and qualitative skills.

Harris & Harris is a premier, full-service revenue recovery firm headquartered and founded in Chicago, IL. Founded in 1968, we have been in business for more than 50 years, and we specialize in the utilities, government, and healthcare markets.

We take pride in knowing what it takes to turn a call from "average" to "excellent." We have been delighting clients and customers for decades thanks to our outstanding employees. They make the difference every day, shift, and call and transform challenges into victories.
At Harris & Harris, we’re proud to be an organization where everyone is welcome and can be their authentic selves at work. Most recently we have partnered with local schools and charitable organizations to give back to our communities including the American Heart Association, Habitat for Humanity, A Just Harvest, and R. Nathaniel Dett Elementary School.
At Harris & Harris, everyone is important, and one person can make a difference for their colleagues, for our clients, and for our company. We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager - Power Delivery
jobs.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

The Senior Power Delivery Project Manager provides technical, administrative, and commercial project management leadership for the development, execution, delivery, and monitoring of Power Delivery projects, including electric transmission, distribution, and substation initiatives, within a defined geographic region, utility client base, or technical discipline. Supports utility capital programs and Power Delivery portfolios by ensuring all responsibilities across the full project lifecycle—including proposal development, project planning and startup, engineering coordination, procurement, construction execution, schedule and cost control, reporting, and project closeout—are executed, documented, and audited in accordance with WSP project management standards, Power Delivery best practices, and client requirements. Provides practical leadership, process improvement, and innovative solutions to address schedule, cost, risk, quality, and stakeholder management challenges within a dynamic, regulated, and evolving Power Delivery and energy infrastructure environment.

This position will be based out of Texas or Louisiana with the ability to work remotely from any mutually acceptable location in the southeast region. You must have the ability to travel to a WSP and/or Client office for periodic face to face meetings.

As one of the world’s leading professional services firms, WSP now brings world-class expertise in power delivery and project management with the recent acquisition of POWER Engineers, Inc. Our vision is to be the preeminent pure-play global consulting firm for the world’s energy transition. And we need your help.

Your Impact

Provide Power Delivery project management leadership for large‑scale and complex utility infrastructure projects, ensuring clear task ownership, schedule accountability, and delivery milestones across transmission, distribution, and substation scopes; prepare and manage project budgets, forecasts, margins, KPIs, earned value, hours and expenses, monitor external risks and contingencies, and ensure contractual compliance and successful delivery of assigned Power Delivery project portfolios.
Develop and execute stakeholder engagement and communication strategies for utility clients, internal leadership, engineering teams, contractors, and regulators, maintaining strong relationships and providing timely reporting on project status, risks, and performance. [
Provide guidance during pursuit, initiation, and project startup phases, supporting Go/No‑Go decisions, contract and commercial reviews, pricing strategies, delivery risk assessments, and mitigation planning for Power Delivery and utility capital projects
Participate in and support the technical and commercial aspects of contract negotiations, client presentations, scope alignment discussions, and project execution meetings with IOUs, IPPs, cooperatives, and public power clients.
Actively lead and enforce appropriate technical and constructability reviews, ensuring selection of qualified engineering and discipline leads, adherence to QA/QC programs, and compliance with utility standards and WSP project quality plans.
Provide written and verbal technical input to multi‑disciplinary Power Delivery project teams and contribute strategic, risk‑informed advisory guidance to clients on schedule, cost, constructability, and execution strategy.
Mentor and coach project managers, engineers, and support staff, supporting career development, performance improvement, and leadership growth within the Power Delivery organization.
Manage, evaluate, and provide performance leadership to assigned staff, ensuring alignment with project objectives, safety expectations, and delivery standards
Ensure timely updates and governance compliance for project management systems and documentation, including Risk Registers (REF/RMP), Project Management Plans (PMP), Quality Plans (QP), Project Safety Plans (PSP), and Communications Plans
Facilitate and lead project kick‑off, safety, and execution alignment meetings with key internal and external stakeholders to establish roles, responsibilities, and delivery expectations.
Coordinate with area managers, technical leads, and resource managers to address staffing, subcontracting, and specialty support needs in a timely manner across Power Delivery programs.
Maintain regular client communications, including monthly progress reporting, safety performance, major risks/issues, and scope or budget impacts, reinforcing WSP’s role as a trusted Power Delivery advisor.
Participate in and lead problem project and recovery reviews, conducting root‑cause analysis, identifying corrective actions, and developing project recovery and mitigation plans
Ensure consistent project reporting and governance updates to clients, technical leadership, and business unit managers, proactively identifying emerging scope, schedule, cost, or risk issues.
Monitor and manage accounts receivable (AR), unbilled revenue, cash flow, and invoicing, coordinating with project accounting and finance teams to resolve issues and maintain financial health of Power Delivery projects.
Complete formal project closeout activities, including financial closeout, documentation archiving, client acceptance, and lessons‑learned workshops to support continuous improvement. [
Remain current on project management best practices, PMAP methodologies, utility delivery trends, and Power Delivery industry standards
Collaborate with cross‑disciplinary professionals to deliver integrated, future‑ready power delivery solutions, strengthening WSP’s position as a trusted advisor to utility clients.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision‑making regarding company funds, client commitments, project risks, and professional conduct, in accordance with WSP’s Code of Conduct and corporate policies.
Perform additional responsibilities as required

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Electrical, Civil, Mechanical), Engineering Technology, Physical Sciences, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent professional experience within an A/E/C, utility, EPC, or power delivery consulting environment.
15+ years of progressive post‑education experience in a project management or senior technical leadership role, preferably supporting power delivery, transmission & distribution (T&D), substation, or utility capital projects.
Highly proficient understanding of the project delivery lifecycle within the A/E/C and utility industries, including proposal development, project initiation, engineering coordination, procurement support, construction execution, commissioning, and project closeout, with a strong background in Power Delivery project management
Advanced analytical and organizational skills with demonstrated business and commercial acumen, enabling effective integration of project controls, financial performance, risk management, and client objectives.
Advanced proficiency in critical thinking, risk‑based decision‑making, and problem‑solving, including performing project management assessments, schedule and cost evaluations, forecasting, and scenario analysis to optimize Power Delivery project outcomes.
Advanced interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to engage effectively, persuasively, and professionally with executive leadership, utility clients (IOUs, IPPs, Co‑Ops, Munis), subcontractors, consultants, and internal teams.
Demonstrated self‑leadership and accountability, with strong attention to detail, quality, multitasking, and adaptability in a fast‑paced Power Delivery and utility project environment.
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision while providing technical guidance, mentoring, and leadership to mid‑level and senior project staff, with strict adherence to QA/QC, safety, and delivery standards.
Advanced proficiency in technical writing, project documentation, office automation, and project management software, including Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Visio, Project, SharePoint), scheduling tools, and Power Delivery PM platforms.
Strong experience managing the review, approval, and coordination of discipline‑specific deliverables, technical reports, scopes of work, and execution plans within a multi‑project, multi‑disciplinary Power Delivery portfolio.
Demonstrated ability to influence and gain cooperation from a broad range of stakeholders, including senior leadership, utility clients, subcontractors, consultants, and matrixed internal teams, without formal authority.
Proven commitment to workplace health, safety, and environmental performance, including adherence to WSP safety programs, drug/alcohol policies, and harassment‑free workplace standards.
Strong ability to adapt to changing project demands, including flexible schedules, outage‑driven work, and evolving client priorities common in Power Delivery and utility capital programs.
Willingness to support occasional travel to client sites, regional offices, and project locations as required to support Power Delivery project execution and client engagement.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s Degree in Engineering.
Essential project management certification (e.g., PMP, CAP-M).
Registered Professional Engineer (PE License)

About WSP

ABOUT US

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. Dedicated to serving local communities, we are engineers, planners, technical experts, strategic advisors and construction management professionals. WSP USA designs lasting solutions in the buildings, transportation, energy, water and environment markets. With more than 15,000 employees in over 300 offices across the U.S., we partner with our clients to help communities prosper.

www.wsp.com

WSP provides a flexible and agile workplace model while meeting client needs. Employees are also afforded a comprehensive suite of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, life, and retirement savings focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career.

At WSP, we want to give our employees the challenges they seek to grow their careers and knowledge base. Your daily contributions to your team will be essential in meeting client objectives, goals and challenges. Are you ready to get started?

WSP USA (and all of its U.S. companies) is an Equal Opportunity Employer Race/Age/Color/Religion/Sex/Sexual Orientation/Gender Identity/National Origin/Disability or Protected Veteran Status.

The selected candidate must be authorized to work in the United States.

NOTICE TO THIRD PARTY AGENCIES:

Unsolicited resumes include any resume or hiring document sent to WSP in the absence of a signed Service Agreement where WSP has expressly requested recruitment/staffing services specific to the position at hand. You will be working on a flexible hybrid schedule as part of Fidelity’s dynamic working arrangement.

The work location for this role is 483 Bay Street in Toronto until approximately late 2026, when the work location will change to the new Mississauga office at 3 Robert Speck Parkway.

Current work authorization for Canada is required for all openings.

Who We Are

At Fidelity, we’ve been helping Canadian investors build better financial futures for over 35 years. We offer individuals and institutions a range of trusted investment portfolios and services - and we’re constantly seeking to find new and better ways to help our clients. As a privately owned company, we boldly embrace innovation in all areas as we continue to grow our business into the future.

Working with us means you’ll be part of a diverse and dedicated group of people who make a real difference for our clients and communities every day. You’ll have a wide range of opportunities to grow and develop your career in an inclusive environment where you’ll feel valued and supported to be your best - both personally and expertly.

Business Overview

Fidelity Clearing Canada (FCC) is the leading independent clearing broker and custodian in the Canadian market. We provide trade execution, clearing, custody and back-office support services to Canadian-based brokerage firms and the Canadian brokerage arms of U.S.-based firms. Fidelity Clearing Canada’s core values for solution delivery are centered around transparency, leadership, and collaboration.

What You Will Do

The Project Manager will support the planning and delivery of FCC’s core digital platform and associated initiatives. The Project Manager will be responsible for successful planning and execution of cross-functional initiatives that define and deliver solutions to meet business needs, tackle business problems and develop new service and product offerings to our clients. Fidelity Clearing initiatives drive scalability, innovation, and continuous improvement of our services in the Canadian Marketplace. The ideal candidate is an adaptable professional, with an entrepreneurial mindset, a high degree of initiative; comfortable in fast-paced, dynamic, and highly collaborative environment.

Strategizing on delivery approach with business stakeholders, and leadership
Developing and executing on a plan with key achievements and clear deliverables and timelines

Working and presenting with senior management and C-level executives and clients

jobs.description:
A Day in the Life of a Project Manager

As a Project Manager, you'll start your day by reviewing active projects, priorities, budgets, and schedules to ensure work is progressing toward successful and profitable completion. You'll manage projects valued over $100K within a single business line, overseeing daily activities and coordinating teams, resources, and timelines. You'll evaluate scopes of work, monitor project costs, and ensure quality standards are consistently met while keeping customers and stakeholders informed throughout the project lifecycle.

Throughout the day, you'll work closely with field teams, customers, subcontractors, and internal partners to address challenges and keep projects moving forward. You'll review Xactimate scopes, evaluate project requirements, and use your knowledge of local, state, and federal codes and inspection requirements to ensure work is completed correctly and in compliance with applicable standards. When unexpected issues arise, you'll use your problem-solving skills to develop solutions while balancing scope, budget, schedule, quality, and customer expectations.

Safety will be a priority in everything you do. You'll ensure delivery teams follow safe work practices and applicable First Onsite and legislative safety requirements, while making sure appropriately trained and deployed trades have the resources they need to perform their work safely. You'll communicate project expectations, monitor progress, and hold teams accountable for delivering quality results. Every day, your leadership will bring together people, planning, technical expertise, and financial oversight to deliver successful projects that meet customer needs and support the profitability of First Onsite.

Responsibilities

Manage projects from start to finish, including full oversight and quality control
Develop and maintain project schedules, timelines, and budgets
Review, approve, and manage subcontractor proposals, scopes, and change orders
Maintain all project documentation: daily logs, reports, inventories, and records
Coordinate with leadership on scope, buy-outs, and reserves
Perform billing reviews, audits, and invoicing
Monitor project risks and proactively address schedule or budget issues
Respond to on-call needs and manage technician/subcontractor availability, 24/7
Fill in as needed, including hands-on tasks and additional responsibilities

2+ years as Assistant Project Manager
Skilled in construction drawings, specs, and take-offs
Supervised 2+ Area Wide Events
Experience in DR or GC
High school diploma or equivalent

Valid driver's license

jobs.description:
Procon is a top-ranked construction management and technology consulting firm with 25 years of experience delivering high—impact projects across the U.S. and worldwide. An ENR Top 100 CM/PM firm, we specialize in program management, project controls, commissioning, and technology--and offer an excellent platform to grow your career while shaping the future of the built environment.

Procon seeks an experienced Construction Project Manager / Quality Assurance Manager / Inspector to support a Fire Alarm replacement at an occupied IRS Service Center Complex in Memphis TN. This on-site role will provide project management and quality assurance construction inspection oversight, helping ensure work is completed safely and in accordance with contract documents approved plans, specifications, and applicable codes and regulations.

This position does not offer employment visa sponsorship. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship.

Requirements

Qualifications & Skills

Minimum of 10 years of construction industry experience, preferably in construction inspection, QA/QC, construction management, or Owner’s Representative roles.
Fire alarm system training and NICET Level II or III in Fire Alarm Systems, IAEI, or ICC/CEI certification required.
Knowledge of applicable state and local codes, IFC and NFPA standards, and fire/life safety requirements.
Previous experience as a Construction Inspector, QA/QC Inspector, QA/QC Manager, or similar field-based construction professional.
Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, or a related discipline preferred, but not required.
Strong knowledge of construction practices, materials, installation methods, quality standards, and OSHA safety requirements.
Experience inspecting architectural, structural, MEP, fire/life safety, and other construction disciplines.
Ability to interpret and apply construction drawings, specifications, and contract documents in the field.
Strong Owner’s Representative and on-site construction management experience, including inspections, RFIs, submittals, schedules, change orders, pay applications, quality control, and contract administration.
Ability to identify discrepancies, construction deficiencies, project risks, and potential safety concerns and coordinate appropriate resolution.
Strong communication and coordination skills with owners, government representatives, contractors, A/E teams, consultants, and other project stakeholders.
Ability to work occasional off-hours and weekends based on construction schedules and project requirements.
Experience managing construction within occupied, operational, or secure facilities; federal, GSA, or other government facility experience highly desirable.
Roofing and occupied federal facility project experience is a plus.
Experience with federal construction processes and documentation, including IGEs, SOWs, acquisition support, commissioning, and project closeout preferred.

Responsibilities & Duties

Serve as the on-site Construction Project Manager and Owner’s Representative, providing daily oversight of construction activities and contractor performance.
Inspect architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and life-safety work for compliance with contract documents, approved submittals, applicable codes, quality standards, and project requirements.
Manage RFIs, submittals, schedules, change orders, pay applications, testing, inspections, project logs, and construction documentation.
Review contractor schedules, progress, change proposals, and payment applications for accuracy and consistency with observed field conditions.
Lead project meetings, prepare meeting minutes, track action items, and coordinate with owners, government representatives, contractors, A/E teams, commissioning agents, and consultants.
Monitor contractor quality control, safety, security, and environmental compliance, including applicable OSHA requirements.
Identify, document, and track deficiencies and non-conforming work through corrective action and resolution.
Evaluate workmanship, materials, installation methods, and construction progress to verify compliance with drawings, specifications, and approved project requirements.
Prepare daily field reports, inspection records, non-conformance notices, photographic documentation, risk assessments, technical briefings, IGEs, SOWs, and other required project deliverables.
Proactively identify and communicate schedule, cost, quality, safety, and field-related risks.
Support contract administration and serve as a liaison between government representatives, contractors, design professionals, and other project stakeholders.
Support project closeout, including punch-list inspections, corrective work verification, testing, commissioning observations, warranties, as-built documentation, final inspections, and turnover.

Physical Requirements

This Position Requires Regular Onsite Presence In An Active Construction Environment. The Employee Must Be Able To Perform The Essential Functions Of The Position, With Or Without Reasonable Accommodation, Including

Walking and standing for extended periods while performing site observations and inspections.
Navigating active construction areas, including stairs, uneven surfaces, temporary walkways, and varying elevations.
Occasionally bending, stooping, kneeling, crouching, reaching, and climbing as necessary to observe construction activities.
Accessing mechanical, electrical, utility, process, and other construction areas as required.

Working in indoor and outdoor environments with exposure to typical construction-site conditions, including noise, dust, weather, and temperature fluctuations.

Salary commensurate with experience.

jobs.title: Program Manager - Maternal Child Health (MCH)
jobs.location: Port Moresby, National Capital District, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
Program Manager, MCH
Reports to:       Country Director

Location:          Port Moresby (up to 20% Provincial Travel)

Background The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low- and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.
CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work in conjunction with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.
At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skillsets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org
CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds and culture.
Program Overview CHAI has been supporting the Ministry of Health in PNG since 2005, working across HIV, immunization, malaria, nutrition, non-communicable diseases (NCDs), and broader health system strengthening. This long-standing partnership reflects CHAI’s commitment to sustainable, government-led health system improvements in PNG.
CHAI’s support for the MCH program began in 2019 and has focused primarily on immunization and nutrition. Over the past six years, CHAI has worked closely with the Government of PNG to set program priorities and drive strategic improvements. Key achievements include spearheading the development of the National Immunisation Strategy, supporting the government to conduct a comprehensive zero-dose analysis, and providing instrumental technical and programmatic support in close collaboration with government and other partners.
PNG continues to face significant maternal and child health challenges, including uneven immunization coverage, difficult service delivery contexts, and constrained sub-national capacity. As the Government of PNG implements its National Immunisation Strategy and prepares for the introduction of new vaccines while strengthening routine immunization and primary health care, CHAI is expanding its support at both national and provincial levels. This includes providing hands-on implementation support in select provinces, strengthening government planning and coordination systems, and building sustainable capacity for improved MCH service delivery.
Position Summary CHAI is seeking a Program Manager for MCH to provide leadership for CHAI’s MCH cluster in PNG, covering the Immunization and Nutrition programs. This role will provide strategic leadership, technical oversight, and project management for the cluster.
The ideal candidate is a credible program leader who excels at managing high-performing teams, overseeing grant implementation and nurturing deep trusted relationships with government partners. We are specifically seeking a candidate with strong monitoring and evaluation capabilities, technical capabilities and exceptional project management skills. The position requires someone who can engage confidently with senior government counterparts, lead complex vaccine and immunization workstreams, and support effective implementation at provincial level.
Reporting to the Country Director, the Program Manager will have day-to-day leadership responsibility for CHAI’s MCH portfolio and will be responsible for growing it. The Program Manager will directly set and manage the program workplan, manage the budget, monitor performance and report to donors, and manage relationships with government and donors. The role requires balancing strategic thinking with hands-on program management, ensuring strong execution while also shaping the future direction and growth of CHAI’s MCH work in PNG.
Performance in this role is reviewed monthly against the role’s accountability scorecard.
Key Responsibilities § Serve as CHAI’s primary day-to-day counterpart to the National EPI Program and National Nutrition Program within the National Department of Health, keeping the engagement log current and holding a weekly HPV and AIHSS huddle.
§ Build and maintain strong, respectful working relationships with senior government officials, Provincial Health Authorities and key partners.
§ Represent CHAI in national and sub-national technical working groups, coordination forums and joint reviews.
§ Provide leadership, mentoring and support to the MCH team, ensuring staff receive timely guidance and support to address challenges, with issues escalated when necessary. Foster a supportive team culture grounded in accountability and learning.
§ Oversee the program budget, monitor utilization, flag potential over- and underspends early, and ensure program requests are reviewed and approved promptly.
§ Ensure high-quality program delivery in line with donor commitments, manage donor relationships, and lead the development of concept notes and proposals as the portfolio evolves.
§ Lead the planning, implementation and monitoring of CHAI’s MCH workplan, including annual operational plans and Nutrition and AIHSS deliverables, ensuring alignment with government priorities and drawing on CHAI’s global technical expertise where relevant.
§ Provide hands-on management of CHAI’s support to routine immunization service delivery, including outreach, supervision and performance improvement at provincial level.
§ Lead CHAI’s technical and programmatic support for new vaccine introductions, including the introduction roadmap, readiness planning, coordination and implementation.
§ Support the Government of PNG to operationalize and roll out the National Immunization Strategy, translating national priorities into practical implementation plans.
§ Oversee CHAI’s support to the National Nutrition Program, ensuring effective coordination and implementation, including timely payment of village health assistants and regular supportive supervision.
§ Work closely with the Country Director to translate strategic direction into practical workplans and measurable results.
§ Contribute to shaping the future direction and growth of CHAI’s MCH portfolio by identifying emerging priorities, gaps and opportunities for impact, in line with CHAI’s regional and global strategies.
§ Identify implementation risks and operational challenges and develop practical mitigation measures.
§ Ensure program data is used effectively to inform decision-making, monitor progress and guide course correction.
§ Lead the preparation of clear, high-quality reports and updates for government counterparts, donors and CHAI leadership, including a one-page monthly report to the Country Director.
§ Share key lessons and risks from PNG with regional and global counterparts to inform CHAI’s broader strategy and learning.
§ Support other organization-wide priorities as assigned by the Country Director.
§ Uphold CHAI’s values and standards of professionalism and accountability and contribute to internal leadership initiatives and cross-team problem-solving.
Qualifications ·      Master’s degree in public health, health sciences, or a health-related field.
·      Minimum of 7 years of relevant professional experience in public health or development, with demonstrated responsibility for program leadership and delivery.
·      Strong experience in vaccines and immunization, including service delivery and new vaccine introduction; nutrition experience is an asset.
·      Strong monitoring and evaluation skills, including experience designing M&E frameworks, analyzing program data, and using evidence to drive program improvements.
·      Demonstrated excellence in stakeholder management and relationship-building, particularly with government partners in complex, multi-stakeholder environments.
·      Proven experience working closely with government counterparts in low-resource or complex settings.
·      Demonstrated ability to lead teams, manage multiple workstreams, and support field-based implementation, including managing managers and provincial teams.
·      Strong financial and grant management skills, including managing a donor-funded portfolio against clear performance measures and raising risks early.
·      Strong judgment, maturity, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to earn credibility and trust with senior stakeholders.
·      Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

Description

Alutiiq Solutions, LLC is seeking a highly qualified and experienced Program Manager to lead and oversee facility operations under the Consolidated Facility Services (CFS) Task Order for the Department of State. This position serves as the single point of contact with the Government and is responsible for overall contract performance, including operations, maintenance, staffing, compliance, and performance management. The role integrates program management and day-to-day operational execution to deliver efficient, compliant, and mission-ready facility services aligned with Department of State objectives. This position requires in-person leadership and coordination and cannot be performed remotely.

Job Duties And Responsibilities (Essential Functions)

Serves as the single point of contact (POC) for the Government and is responsible for overall contract performance and execution. This includes ensuring alignment with mission requirements and contractual objectives.
Provides unified leadership across all operational and maintenance functions to ensure efficient, coordinated, and uninterrupted facility operations.
Develops, implements, and maintains the Program Management Plan (PMP), including planning, scheduling, risk management, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Oversees preventive and corrective maintenance activities in alignment with Consolidated Facility Services (CFS) requirements and Reliability Centered Maintenance (RCM) methodologies.
Ensures compliance with all applicable regulations, policies, and safety standards, including federal, state, and Department of State requirements.
Manages contract financial performance, including cost control, resource allocation, and adherence to budgetary constraints.
Supervises contractor personnel and ensures staffing levels, qualifications, and training requirements are met in accordance with contract requirements.
Oversees Work Control and CMMS (Maximo) operations to ensure accurate work order management, preventive maintenance scheduling, and data integrity.
Monitors performance against Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), Acceptable Quality Levels (AQLs), and Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) requirements to ensure contract compliance.
Conducts meetings with Government stakeholders and provides required reports, including performance metrics, safety updates, and operational status.
Oversees Quality Control and Safety programs to ensure compliance with contractual requirements and industry standards.
Coordinates with the Contracting Officer Representative (COR) and other stakeholders to prioritize work and align execution with mission requirements.
Supports specialized services, including environmental compliance and energy management, as required by the contract.

Requirements

Job Description

Are you an AI-forward master of managing complex, cross-functional work? Are you energized by building something that does not yet have a playbook? Are you exceptionally skilled at creating clarity, alignment, momentum, and accountability as the work evolves? Then apply today for this Project Manager Senior, EDU.FYI opportunity!

ASU EdPlus is a dynamic unit of Arizona State University focused on the design and scalable delivery of digital teaching and learning models to increase student success and reduce barriers to achievement in higher education. We advance the economic, social, cultural, and overall health of the local, national, and international communities served by ASU.

Curious about what it’s like to work at EdPlus? Watch this short video, then explore more stories on the EdPlus at ASU YouTube channel.

We are seeking a Project Manager Senior
to support EDU.FYI
, a strategic partnership between ASU and FYI focused on reimagining how people learn, create, and solve problems with artificial intelligence.

FYI is an AI-powered platform and technology company founded by will.i.am, built around the belief that AI should amplify human agency, creativity, and potential. Through EDU.FYI, ASU and FYI are bringing together ASU’s leadership in education and innovation with FYI’s technology to explore a new model for AI-powered learning that moves beyond simply using AI tools to actively build, create, and solve meaningful problems alongside AI.

The highly dynamic, evolving partnership is building and testing new AI-enabled learning experiences, products, and programs designed to help learners develop the skills, mindset, and agency to thrive in an increasingly AI-powered world.

You will play a critical role in turning that ambition into coordinated execution. Every day you will make a difference in the lives of others by bringing structure to ambiguity, translating partnership and leadership priorities into actionable plans, and driving progress across multiple interconnected workstreams spanning technology, academic programming, research, marketing, enrollment, partnerships, and new initiatives. Success in this role requires sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to build alignment and navigate complex stakeholder environments as priorities and organizational needs evolve.

Essential Duties

Project Planning and Execution — 35%

Develop, maintain, and actively manage the integrated EDU.FYI project plan across partnership workstreams, translating priorities and decisions into clear deliverables, owners, milestones, timelines, and next steps.
Drive day-to-day execution against established plans and milestones; maintain project schedules and tools, monitor progress, follow up with owners, and adjust plans as priorities and requirements evolve.

Cross-Functional Coordination and Follow-Through — 30%

Facilitate recurring project working sessions and drive follow-through on decisions and commitments, ensuring clear ownership and proactively surfacing work that is delayed, blocked, or at risk.

Risk, Issue, and Dependency Management — 15%

Proactively identify and track project risks, issues, dependencies, and delivery constraints, working with responsible stakeholders to develop and monitor mitigation plans.
Exercise sound judgment in resolving project issues and stakeholder conflicts at the appropriate level, recognizing when leadership alignment or intervention is required and escalating significant risks, unresolved dependencies, priority conflicts, and decisions to the Director of Enterprise Delivery with clear context and recommended next steps.

Reporting and Partnership Visibility — 15%

Maintain accurate, current visibility into EDU.FYI initiatives and milestones, consolidating workstream updates into concise, decision-ready project status reporting for the Director of Enterprise Delivery and partnership leadership.
Maintain documentation of key decisions, commitments, risks, dependencies, and changes to project scope or timelines, and support executive updates by gathering, validating, and synthesizing complex or sensitive project information for senior stakeholders.

Project Management Infrastructure and Continuous Improvement — 5%

Establish and maintain consistent project management practices, tools, templates, and core governance artifacts, including the integrated roadmap, RACI, project plans, and decision and risk logs.
Identify and implement opportunities to improve operating cadence, workflows, communication, accountability, and scalable project management infrastructure as the partnership evolves.
Assume or coordinate additional duties or projects as assigned or directed.

Bachelor’s degree in business, project management, technology, higher education administration, or a related field.
Experience independently leading complex, cross-functional projects involving multiple teams, senior stakeholders, external partners, and concurrent priorities.
Experience translating broad priorities and objectives into actionable project plans, milestones, owners, and timelines.
Experience building alignment and driving execution and accountability across stakeholders with differing perspectives, priorities, and levels of authority, including without direct supervisory authority.
Experience managing project dependencies, risks, issues, and changing priorities.
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in highly ambiguous environments, bringing structure, clarity, and forward momentum to work where priorities, requirements, or processes are not yet fully defined.
Experience facilitating cross-functional working sessions and driving clear follow-through from meetings and decisions.
Experience communicating with and supporting senior leadership, including synthesizing complex or sensitive information, anticipating stakeholder needs, and tailoring communications to enable timely decisions and alignment.
Demonstrated ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments with sound judgment, discretion, diplomacy, and awareness of organizational context and competing priorities.

Experience working in higher education, technology, digital products, strategic partnerships, or similarly complex environments.
Evidence of strong communication skills, executive-level judgment and discretion, attention to detail, and ability to prioritize effectively in a complex, fast-moving environment.

Describe a complex, cross-functional project or initiative you independently managed involving multiple teams, stakeholders, or concurrent workstreams. How did you translate priorities into an actionable project plan, establish ownership and timelines, and drive accountability through execution?

Job Description

This Opportunity

The Senior Power Delivery Project Manager provides technical, administrative, and commercial project management leadership for the development, execution, delivery, and monitoring of Power Delivery projects, including electric transmission, distribution, and substation initiatives, within a defined geographic region, utility client base, or technical discipline. Supports utility capital programs and Power Delivery portfolios by ensuring all responsibilities across the full project lifecycle—including proposal development, project planning and startup, engineering coordination, procurement, construction execution, schedule and cost control, reporting, and project closeout—are executed, documented, and audited in accordance with WSP project management standards, Power Delivery best practices, and client requirements. Provides practical leadership, process improvement, and innovative solutions to address schedule, cost, risk, quality, and stakeholder management challenges within a dynamic, regulated, and evolving Power Delivery and energy infrastructure environment

This position will be based out of New Orleans, LA with the ability to work remotely from any mutually acceptable location in the region. You must have the ability to travel to a WSP and/or Client office for periodic face to face meetings.

As one of the world’s leading professional services firms, WSP now brings world-class expertise in power delivery and project management with the recent acquisition of POWER Engineers, Inc. Our vision is to be the preeminent pure-play global consulting firm for the world’s energy transition. And we need your help.

Your Impact

Provide Power Delivery project management leadership for large‑scale and complex utility infrastructure projects, ensuring clear task ownership, schedule accountability, and delivery milestones across transmission, distribution, and substation scopes; prepare and manage project budgets, forecasts, margins, KPIs, earned value, hours and expenses, monitor external risks and contingencies, and ensure contractual compliance and successful delivery of assigned Power Delivery project portfolios.
Develop and execute stakeholder engagement and communication strategies for utility clients, internal leadership, engineering teams, contractors, and regulators, maintaining strong relationships and providing timely reporting on project status, risks, and performance. [
Provide guidance during pursuit, initiation, and project startup phases, supporting Go/No‑Go decisions, contract and commercial reviews, pricing strategies, delivery risk assessments, and mitigation planning for Power Delivery and utility capital projects
Participate in and support the technical and commercial aspects of contract negotiations, client presentations, scope alignment discussions, and project execution meetings with IOUs, IPPs, cooperatives, and public power clients.
Actively lead and enforce appropriate technical and constructability reviews, ensuring selection of qualified engineering and discipline leads, adherence to QA/QC programs, and compliance with utility standards and WSP project quality plans.
Provide written and verbal technical input to multi‑disciplinary Power Delivery project teams and contribute strategic, risk‑informed advisory guidance to clients on schedule, cost, constructability, and execution strategy.
Mentor and coach project managers, engineers, and support staff, supporting career development, performance improvement, and leadership growth within the Power Delivery organization.
Manage, evaluate, and provide performance leadership to assigned staff, ensuring alignment with project objectives, safety expectations, and delivery standards
Ensure timely updates and governance compliance for project management systems and documentation, including Risk Registers (REF/RMP), Project Management Plans (PMP), Quality Plans (QP), Project Safety Plans (PSP), and Communications Plans
Facilitate and lead project kick‑off, safety, and execution alignment meetings with key internal and external stakeholders to establish roles, responsibilities, and delivery expectations.
Coordinate with area managers, technical leads, and resource managers to address staffing, subcontracting, and specialty support needs in a timely manner across Power Delivery programs.
Maintain regular client communications, including monthly progress reporting, safety performance, major risks/issues, and scope or budget impacts, reinforcing WSP’s role as a trusted Power Delivery advisor.
Participate in and lead problem project and recovery reviews, conducting root‑cause analysis, identifying corrective actions, and developing project recovery and mitigation plans
Ensure consistent project reporting and governance updates to clients, technical leadership, and business unit managers, proactively identifying emerging scope, schedule, cost, or risk issues.
Monitor and manage accounts receivable (AR), unbilled revenue, cash flow, and invoicing, coordinating with project accounting and finance teams to resolve issues and maintain financial health of Power Delivery projects.
Complete formal project closeout activities, including financial closeout, documentation archiving, client acceptance, and lessons‑learned workshops to support continuous improvement. [
Remain current on project management best practices, PMAP methodologies, utility delivery trends, and Power Delivery industry standards
Collaborate with cross‑disciplinary professionals to deliver integrated, future‑ready power delivery solutions, strengthening WSP’s position as a trusted advisor to utility clients.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision‑making regarding company funds, client commitments, project risks, and professional conduct, in accordance with WSP’s Code of Conduct and corporate policies.
Perform additional responsibilities as required

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Electrical, Civil, Mechanical), Engineering Technology, Physical Sciences, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent professional experience within an A/E/C, utility, EPC, or power delivery consulting environment.
12+ years of progressive post‑education experience in a project management or senior technical leadership role, preferably supporting power delivery, transmission & distribution (T&D), substation, or utility capital projects.
Highly proficient understanding of the project delivery lifecycle within the A/E/C and utility industries, including proposal development, project initiation, engineering coordination, procurement support, construction execution, commissioning, and project closeout, with a strong background in Power Delivery project management
Advanced analytical and organizational skills with demonstrated business and commercial acumen, enabling effective integration of project controls, financial performance, risk management, and client objectives.
Advanced proficiency in critical thinking, risk‑based decision‑making, and problem‑solving, including performing project management assessments, schedule and cost evaluations, forecasting, and scenario analysis to optimize Power Delivery project outcomes.
Advanced interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to engage effectively, persuasively, and professionally with executive leadership, utility clients (IOUs, IPPs, Co‑Ops, Munis), subcontractors, consultants, and internal teams.
Demonstrated self‑leadership and accountability, with strong attention to detail, quality, multitasking, and adaptability in a fast‑paced Power Delivery and utility project environment.
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision while providing technical guidance, mentoring, and leadership to mid‑level and senior project staff, with strict adherence to QA/QC, safety, and delivery standards.
Advanced proficiency in technical writing, project documentation, office automation, and project management software, including Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Visio, Project, SharePoint), scheduling tools, and Power Delivery PM platforms.
Strong experience managing the review, approval, and coordination of discipline‑specific deliverables, technical reports, scopes of work, and execution plans within a multi‑project, multi‑disciplinary Power Delivery portfolio.
Demonstrated ability to influence and gain cooperation from a broad range of stakeholders, including senior leadership, utility clients, subcontractors, consultants, and matrixed internal teams, without formal authority.
Proven commitment to workplace health, safety, and environmental performance, including adherence to WSP safety programs, drug/alcohol policies, and harassment‑free workplace standards.
Strong ability to adapt to changing project demands, including flexible schedules, outage‑driven work, and evolving client priorities common in Power Delivery and utility capital programs.
Willingness to support occasional travel to client sites, regional offices, and project locations as required to support Power Delivery project execution and client engagement.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s Degree in Engineering.
Essential project management certification (e.g., PMP, CAP-M).

jobs.title: Senior, Business Analyst
jobs.description:
WHY DEPT®?

We are pioneers at heart. What this means, is that we are always leaning forward, thinking of what we can create tomorrow that does not exist today. We were born digital and we are a new model of agency, with a deep skillset in tech and marketing. That’s why we hire curious, self-driven, talented people who never stop innovating.

Our culture is big enough to cope and small enough to care. Meaning, that with people across 20+ countries, we’re big enough to provide you with the best tools, global opportunities, and benefits that help you thrive. While acting small by investing in you, your growth, your team, and giving you the autonomy to solve our clients’ problems, no matter where you are in the world.

THE ROLE

DEPT® is looking for a Business Analyst who owns a workstream independently. A Senior Business Analyst at DEPT leads the translation of complex business needs into actionable product and technology solutions. They'll work across clients, strategists, product managers, designers, engineers, and QA teams, to create alignment from discovery through delivery and ensure that solutions address the intended business and user outcomes, all with minimal oversight. Our business analysts move between clients, industries, and delivery models, balancing client expectations against delivery constraints while working inside multidisciplinary agency teams.

GenAI fluency is core to this role, and you'll be expected to use AI tools daily, including drafting requirements and user stories, summarizing discovery sessions, generating first-pass documentation, all while applying the judgment built through years or rigor to critically review and correct the output, rather than trusting it blindly. Additionally, a good candidate for this role should have a willingness to push the field forward, eager to create new ways of using these tools to build clarity for their teams.

What You'll Own

Requirements and acceptance criteria for your workstream, start to finish
Traceability from business goals through requirements, stories, and delivered outcomes
Stakeholder alignment on scope and expected outcomes
UAT strategy, including scenarios, readiness criteria, and validation

What You'll Do

Run Discovery: Lead stakeholder interviews and workshops, turning what you hear into clear, testable requirements and user stories.
Document Process & Gaps: Map current and future-state processes — flowcharts, personas, use cases, data mappings — and close gaps before they hit delivery.
Work the Team's Cadence: Follow Agile/Scrum or Kanban practices, adapting to the team's rhythm.
Resolve Stakeholder Conflict: Build trust-based relationships and resolve conflicting priorities directly, translating between technical and business language.
Define the Details: Business rules, data requirements, integrations, dependencies, and exception scenarios.
Mentorship: Guide junior team members on documentation standards and technique.

What You Bring

Independent Ownership: 2–4 years of BA experience, with a track record of owning a workstream independently rather than assisting under a senior BA.
Information Gathering & Documentation: Comfort running discovery and producing user stories, acceptance criteria, process diagrams, and functional specs.
Methodology: Working knowledge of Agile and the Software Development Lifecycle.
Tools: Proficiency with Jira, Confluence, Lucidchart, Miro, FigJam, and/or Adobe Workfront.
Platform Exposure: Familiarity with platforms like the Adobe stack (especially AEM), Salesforce (especially Commerce Cloud), and CMS platforms like Contentful or Optimizely a plus.
Agency Experience: Comfort moving between clients, industries, and delivery models in multidisciplinary teams, while balancing client expectations against delivery constraints. Ideal candidates will have experience working in Advertising.
Education: Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, IT, Computer Science, or related field, or equivalent practical experience.

How You Work

Clear Communication: Adjust the level of detail for executives, clients, or engineers as needed.
Facilitation & Curiosity: Run workshops that end in decisions, not just discussion, and ask the question that gets past the stated ask to the real problem.
Influence & Judgment: Build alignment through evidence and clear tradeoffs, and push back on unclear requirements or shaky solutions, respectfully but directly.
Ownership & Adaptability: Flag risks early, document decisions, and stay effective when priorities or teams shift under you.
Coaching: Give junior analysts real, actionable feedback.

What Success Looks Like

Early Risk Detection: Risks, assumptions, and dependencies surface early.
Documentation: Decisions and changes are documented clearly.
UAT: Validates business outcomes, not just feature completion.
Mentorship: Junior analysts get consistent guidance and feedback.

WHAT DO WE OFFER?

We enjoy spending time together, working closely with other local colleagues, and getting to know one another. Our Buenos Aires offices (Villa Crespo or Mar del Plata) are fully equipped with refreshments and great common spaces!
Premium healthcare through OSDE for the employee and their immediate family members
Mendel prepaid card with a monthly allowance for grocery purchases
Monthly reimbursements for Wi-Fi/electricity expenses
Monthly reimbursements for training/English classes
100% covered “Plan Total” membership at Sportclub
Access to our benefits platform through Bonda
A flexible vacation policy

WE SUPPORT YOU BEING YOU

DEPT® is an equal opportunity employer (EOE). We believe our work is at its best when our people feel safe and free to be themselves. We’re committed to an inclusive and barrier-free recruitment and selection process and workplace, regardless of anyone’s lived experience, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, and genetic information. So tell us about any accommodations you need. It’s totally confidential and only used to make sure you feel fully supported at every step.

We are a B Corp-certified company passionate about purpose-driven work. Our hope is that you can feel good about the contributions DEPT® is making to the world, and we always have an open door for your ideas in making the world a better place.

DEPT® is a pioneering technology and marketing services company that creates integrated end-to-end digital experiences for brands such as Google, KFC, Philips, Audi, Twitch, Patagonia, eBay and more. Its team of 2,500+ digital specialists across 30+ locations on 5 continents delivers pioneering work on a global scale with a boutique culture.

Learn more about DEPT®

DIVERSITY, EQUITY, & INCLUSION

At DEPT®, we take pride in creating an inclusive workplace where everyone has an equal opportunity to thrive. We actively seek to recruit, develop, nurture, and retain talented individuals from diverse backgrounds, with varying skills and perspectives.

Not sure you meet all qualifications? Apply, and let us decide! Research shows that women and members of underrepresented groups tend not to apply for jobs when they think they may not meet every requirement, when in fact they do. We believe in giving everyone a fair chance to shine.

We also encourage you to reach out to us and discuss any reasonable adjustments we can make to support you throughout the recruitment process and your time with us.

jobs.description:
Company

Cogent Communications is a global, Tier 1 facilities-based ISP, consistently ranked as one of the top five networks in the world and is publicly traded on the NASDAQ Stock Market under the ticker symbol CCOI. Cogent specializes in providing businesses with high speed Internet access and Ethernet transport services. Cogent's facilities-based, all-optical IP network backbone provides IP services globally. Since its inception, Cogent has unleashed the benefits of IP technology, building one of the largest and highest capacity IP networks in the world. This network enables Cogent to offer large bandwidth connections at highly competitive prices. Cogent also offers superior customer support by virtue of its end-to-end control of service delivery and network monitoring. A competitive base salary and a full benefits package including; Health, Dental, Vision, Paid Time Off (PTO), Short and Long Term Disability, Life Insurance, Holidays, Parental Leave, 401(k) plan with employer match, stock options, and an Employee Assistance Program. Most benefits take effect within 30 days of employment, and some require a waiting period.

Job Summary

The Cybersecurity Analyst (Security & AI Governance)
is responsible for protecting the organization's information assets, technology infrastructure, applications, cloud environments, data, and artificial intelligence (AI) initiatives from cyber threats and misuse. This role serves as a key contributor to both cybersecurity operations and AI governance programs by identifying, assessing, monitoring, and mitigating risks associated with Information Systems as well as AI-enabled technologies.

The Cybersecurity Analyst (Security & AI Governance) works closely with IT teams, software developers, business stakeholders, and external partners to ensure cybersecurity and AI initiatives align with security policies, industry standards, regulatory requirements, and emerging AI governance frameworks. This position will work closely with the CIO/CISO functions to provide a cohesive plan for cybersecurity initiatives, AI governance, Shadow AI oversight, risk management, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Compensation

[Starting / Initial] Base Salary Pay Range: $110,000 - $130,000

Specific offers within the listed pay ranges are determined by a variety of factors such as experience, education, skills, certifications and business needs.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Monitor security systems, networks, applications, cloud platforms, and AI-enabled services for suspicious activity and potential threats.
Perform security assessments and risk analyses of systems, applications, AI solutions, and business processes.
Assist in the development, implementation, and continuous improvements of cybersecurity and AI governance policies, standards, procedures, and controls.
Collaborate with IT, software development, and business teams to implement security best practices and controls (security-by-design principles and secure technology solutions)
Participate in the review, risk assessment, and governance oversight of internally developed AI solutions, machine learning models, and employee-driven AI initiatives.
Evaluate third-party AI vendors, applications, and services for cybersecurity, privacy, compliance, data protection, and operational risks.
Identify, assess, and monitor risks associated with generative AI, large language models (LLMs), machine learning platforms, prompt injection attacks, data leakage, insecure APIs, and AI supply chain vulnerabilities.
Assist with the development and administration of the organization's AI governance and Shadow AI oversight programs.
Support secure development practices for internally developed applications and AI-enabled solutions, and emerging technology initiatives.
Participate in security awareness and AI awareness training initiatives for employees.
Assist with audits, compliance reviews, AI governance assessments, and regulatory reporting requirements.
Research emerging cybersecurity threats, vulnerabilities, cybersecurity trends, AI technologies, and industry best practices and recommend appropriate mitigation strategies/countermeasures.
Maintain inventories of approved AI solutions, AI vendors, and AI-related business initiatives.
Develop and maintain reports, dashboards, metrics, risk assessments, and documentation related to cybersecurity operations, AI governance, compliance and enterprise risk management activities.

Qualifications

Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Information Systems, Computer Science, Risk Management, Business, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
Minimum of 2–5 years of experience in cybersecurity, technology risk, GRC, application security, vendor risk, privacy, IT audit, compliance, technology governance, or a related discipline.
Experience performing technology, security, vendor, application, privacy, or operational risk assessments.
Experience developing, interpreting, implementing, or supporting technology policies, standards, procedures, or governance processes.
Experience evaluating new technologies, applications, vendors, or services from a risk and security perspective.
Experience working collaboratively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document risks and develop recommendations for both technical and executive audiences.
Demonstrated interest in artificial intelligence, generative AI, responsible AI adoption, and emerging technology risk.
Familiarity with generative AI, machine learning concepts, large language models (LLMs), or AI-enabled business applications.

Proficient In The Following Areas

Familiarity with AI governance principles and emerging AI risk management frameworks.
AI governance concepts and risks associated with generative AI technologies.
Data protection, data classification, privacy, and appropriate data use.
Knowledge of application security concepts, API security, and secure software development practices.
Understanding of risks associated with generative AI platforms, LLMs, prompt injection, data privacy, and AI model security.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to independently research emerging technologies and translate findings into practical recommendations.
Ability to write and present formal documentation, risk assessments, and executive-level reports.
Knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks and standards, including CIS Controls, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, and security best practices.
Experience with security information and event management (SIEM) tools and security monitoring platforms is a PLUS.
Experience supporting software development, DevSecOps, or application security initiatives is a PLUS.

Preferred Certifications

Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC)
CompTIA Security+
GIAC Security Essentials (GSEC)
Relevant AI Security, Cloud Security, Application Security, or Governance certifications are highly desirable.

Physical Requirements

Remains in a sitting/stationary position continually or almost continually during the work day
Operates a computer and performs desk-based computer tasks continually; frequently viewing a computer screen
Rarely lifting, carrying, pushing, pulling objects and/or equipment that weighs up to 50 pounds
