You will not design our studios. Our architects do that. You make sure the work gets done. You hold the schedule, keep everyone pointed in the same direction, and buy what we need before we need it. You will carry a project through every phase: design, permitting, bid and award, construction, and closeout.
This is a job for an architect who wants more ownership than a firm will hand them yet. You will see a project from an empty shell to a room full of clients, and you will have your hands on every part of it.
The basics
Title: Project Manager, Design & Construction
Reports to: Chief of Development
Location: Washington, DC area. On site most days, not behind a desk.
Schedule: Full-time, salaried
Pay: $70,000 to $80,000 a year, depending on experience
Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, and staff discounts
Start date: As soon as we find the right person

Coordinating the work
Keep each project on schedule
Hold the schedule for every build-out and know what is holding things up.
Walk the site often enough that you know what is really happening, not what the report says.
Coordinate the subcontractors and trades we hire directly, and watch the places where their work meets, so installation conflicts get caught before they are built.
Tell us early when something slips.

Coordinate the meetings
Write the agenda before each meeting and send it out ahead of time.
Remind people what they need to prepare before each meeting.
Lead the meeting.
Send meeting minutes afterward that say what we decided, what is still open, who owns each item, and when it is due.

Keep everyone moving between meetings
Follow up on open items without being asked.
Everyone on the project should always know what they owe, to whom, and by when.
Chase the quiet ones. A missing answer is the most common reason a job stalls.

Know what to bring to us
Handle the small questions yourself.
Send design and technical questions to the architect, the contractor, or both.
Bring anything that changes cost, schedule, the lease, or how a studio feels to a client to the Chief of Development.
Make our process simpler each time, so we are not starting from scratch on the next studio.

Ordering, permits, and paperwork
Buy what we need, on time
Keep the list of furniture, fixtures, and finishes for each project.
Place orders early enough for long lead times.
Track delivery dates and chase the ones that drift.
Arrange storage and keep what arrives organized and labeled.
Check every delivery for the right size, color, finish, and count.
Handle damaged, missing, and wrong items with the vendor until they are resolved.

Coordinate permits and inspections
Coordinate permit applications in DC, Maryland, and Virginia.
Coordinate inspections and clear whatever inspectors flag.
Keep us on the path to opening on time.

Work with our landlords
Coordinate with landlords during design, so the design team has what it needs to finish the drawings.
Send plans for landlord approval and meet the deadlines in the lease.
Put together the paperwork to draw down our construction allowance.
Check that the space we are given matches what the lease promised.

Watch the money
Keep a running list of change orders.
Check contractor invoices against the work actually finished.
Flag anything that looks wrong before we pay it.
Place orders and approve invoices up to an agreed amount. Anything above that goes to the Chief of Development.

Close projects out properly
Produce the punch list with the architect, and drive it to zero.
Collect as-built drawings, manuals, and warranties.

Keep our vendors in order
Catalogue service contracts and what each vendor owes us under them, including when warranties start and end.
Collect insurance certificates, W-9s, and licenses before work starts.
Make sure the right company name and address is on every contract, permit, and utility account. Each studio is a separate company.

Review the drawings
Read drawing sets closely before they go out to bid.
Catch conflicts between the architectural, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing drawings.
Compare the drawings against what is actually in the space.

Coordinate the bid and award
Put bid packages together and send them to the contractors we want bidding.
Review and level the bids so we are comparing the same scope, not just the same bottom line. Find the exclusions, allowances, and gaps.
Answer bidder questions, and make sure every clarification reaches all of them at once.
Track scope through construction, so we know what each contract covers and what it does not.
Coordinate the RFI process. Log every question, chase the answer, and get the response to the people building from it.

Travel and site time
This job happens on site. You will be at our studios and job sites most days.
You need a car and a valid driver’s license.
You will travel to sites across the greater DC area, up to about a 90-minute drive, as our projects require.
We pay mileage for driving between sites.
Time spent driving between sites during your workday is paid time.

What this grows into
The first year is about coordinating our projects well. After that, there is more.
One Unwind standard. Build the kit we use every time: our treatment room layout, our finishes, our lighting and fixtures, our approved vendors. Right now each studio starts closer to scratch than it needs to. You would own the thing that fixes that.
Opening new studios. Signage, equipment, utilities, internet, and the walkthrough with our operations team before the first client arrives.
Looking after the studios we already have. Repairs, service contracts, and small upgrades across five locations between build-outs.
What we are looking for
You need
A degree in architecture, or a closely related field.
Four to six years of work after school, in a firm, with a contractor, or on the owner’s side, on projects like ours.
The ability to read a full set of drawings and understand how a space gets built.
Clear writing. You will send a lot of agendas, minutes, and vendor emails.
Strong organizational habits.
The patience to follow up on the same open item four times.
A car and a valid driver’s license.

Helpful, but not required
Work on tenant fit-outs or interior build-outs.
Experience with permitting in DC, Maryland, or Virginia.
Experience ordering furniture, fixtures, and finishes, and tracking what arrives.
Spanish.

Software
Revit or AutoCAD
Bluebeam or similar
Procore or similar
Excel or Google Sheets
Slack

What success looks like
In your first 90 days
You have walked every active site and met every architect, contractor, and major vendor we work with.
Every project has one schedule, and you hold it.
Our meetings have agendas before them and minutes after them.
You know what has been ordered, what has not, and what is sitting in storage.

By the end of your first year
Nothing has been held up because an order went in late.
Permits and inspections run on a schedule we can see, not a scramble.
We stopped finding out about problems a week after they happened.
The Chief of Development is spending time on decisions, not on chasing people.

How to apply
Send us a resume and a few lines about a project you helped get built. We would rather hear about one real thing you worked on than read a cover letter.
Send photos of that project too, close enough that we can see how it was put together. We care more about how work was executed than how it was drawn.
Unwind Wellness is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background, and we do not discriminate on any basis protected by law.

new_jobs.description:
Description

Provide support for the implementation of major, highly complex, and mission critical facility management efforts throughout the world. The incumbent’s actions cut across the entire Bureau of Overseas Buildings Operations, Office of Facility Management (OBO/FAC) organization, requiring significant insight, far-reaching coordination, and long term planning both internally and in coordination with other key offices within OBO (e.g. budget, policy, human resources, travel). The work requires management and overview of financial and human resources, administrative support services, organizational policy development and implementation, management controls, special studies and analysis, resource allocation, validation and prioritization of needs, review, approval, and audit of funding, and the establishment of internal operating procedures for OBO/FAC.

Participates as a key member of OBO/FAC’s management team providing guidance and advice to the Office Director and Division Chiefs with regards to establishing and meeting financial, management, and administrative goals and objectives.
Oversees OBO/FAC support services and ensures services meet timely and functional needs of the Office and align fully with OBO’s mandated guidance and procedures; and works closely with other OBO offices to ensure FAC needs support and reflect management decisions.
Provides training to multiple entities on OBO/FAC administrative and financial policies and procedures; serves as the point-of-contact for overseas posts on any questions on the use of OBO/FAC funds; and resolves problems and assists posts in obtaining needed resources.
Conducts research and proposes solutions to organizational inefficiencies and to increase the effectiveness of the organization. Leverages expertise in management and organizational principles pertaining to areas of responsibility (e.g., administrative procedures, financial

management rules and regulations, priorities, etc.) in order to plan and conduct complex studies to assess organizational and financial operations.

Develops and/or recommends edits on facilities management policies. If accepted by the Department, promulgates said policies. Provides expert advice on the administrative and management implications of new program proposals. Drafts updates to 15 FAM to reflect

changes based on the evolving mission and its authorities.

Develops, for consideration by the Department, and reviews internal OBO/FAC initiatives to ensure the orderly, effective, and efficient accomplishment of assigned missions consistent with directives of OBO/FAC and higher Departmental authorities (e.g. New Embassy Transition,

Mechanical Controls Program).

Provides guidance or clarification to posts (e.g., 7901.3 Routine Maintenance and Repair versus 7901.C Maintenance Cost Sharing) on the correct use of facility management funds. Provides input on proposed changes to FAC funding matrices; and guidance on aligning FAC services with

OBO goals and objectives.

Ensures that all documents are well-written, in proper format, timely, complete, and fully coordinates with other affected organizations. Prepare meeting minutes, presentations and reporting documents; the compilation and proper filing of project documents; and the draft

and/or review planning documents.

Assesses the overall progress of funding implementation that is committed or in progress and outlines issues and recommends solutions necessary for senior FAC managers to improve or resolve difficulties, and to ensure funds are obligated and that carry-over is minimized.
Oversees the initiation and accomplishment of administrative office support services (e.g. memorandums for decisions, official requests for information, etc.) functions ensuring they are effectively and efficiently enabling the organization to meet its worldwide commitments.
Develops and maintains yearly and long-range resource needs in line with management priorities; monitors expenditures to ensure availability and correctness of funds; makes projections regarding expenditure patterns; and prepares and reviews financial expenditures,

obligations, and fiscal year close-out reports.

Develops and formulates, for the consideration of the Department, financial and management controls for all Divisions; tracks all funds allotted to posts or allocated to programs to ensure that obligations and liquidations are used appropriately and contract actions are closed-out in a

timely manner; and develops, coordinates, and reviews quarterly and yearly financial updates required by the Department, ensuring that the information is accurate and up-to-date.

Ensures project objectives are met and that resulting recommendations for action are sound and practical and include implementation plans. Follows up to ensure that approved recommendations are successfully implemented

Requirements

CLEARANCE LEVEL: The clearance level (Secret or TS) will be identified in the task order request. Required Qualifications The Program Analyst shall meet the below qualifications. a) Bachelor’s degree b) Six (6) years or more of relevant experience. c) Knowledge and mastery of the application of a wide range of qualitative or quantitative (e.g., using excel spreadsheets, , Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS), Departmental accounting systems) methods for assessing and improving effectiveness. d) Knowledge of the range of financial laws, policies, regulations, and precedents applicable to the Facility Management programs. e) Knowledge and ability to assemble and analyze relevant facts and draw significant conclusions. f) Knowledge and skill in presenting accurate findings and the ability to make feasible and responsive recommendations both orally and in writing. These recommendations may require negotiations with management to accept extensive changes in established procedures or they may involve substantial resources. g) Knowledge and skill in database management, data analytics, and the use of Microsoft Office programs. h) Ability to interact effectively with individuals in garnering cooperation and support for key planning, operations, and management initiatives in the assigned program area. i) Knowledge and ability to design and conduct comprehensive management studies. Desired Qualifications a) Bachelor’s degree in Business, Computer Science or related field is preferred.

new_jobs.title: HR Project Manager - Remote-First
new_jobs.description:
Be part of a movement to change the way Europe pays

In today’s digital Europe, payments still feel too complicated. Random delays, confusing rules, extra apps and accounts make it harder than it should be to pay and get paid.

The European Payments Initiative is changing that with Wero, a proudly European digital wallet to make payments easier, clearer and more secure. Online, in store, at home and across borders, with your money and data protected under European laws and regulations.

Wero is live in Belgium, France and Germany and launching very soon in Luxembourg and the Netherlands. Backed by 16 major banks and the two largest European acquirers, we’re building a brand new, proudly European payment system. Why not join us?

What's in it for you

We operate in a highly regulated industry, which means rigor and structure matter. But that doesn’t mean everything is set in stone. There is still plenty of room to experiment, challenge the way we work and introduce better tools and practices. Our HR team is curious and enthusiastic about opening new topics and trying new approaches.

You’ll work transversally with every part of People and directly with our Chief People Officer, giving you broad exposure to the function and a real opportunity to shape how we work as we continue to grow and mature.

About The Team

You’ll report directly to the Chief People Officer , who oversees HR Operations, Compensation & Benefits, HR Business Partnering and Talent Acquisition. You’ll join a team of 16 international HR experts spread across Europe, each bringing their own expertise and perspective.

We’re still flying the plane while building parts of it, so expect the occasional bumpy ride. The good news? The crew is cheerful, supportive and always ready to help, so you’ll be in safe hands.

Your impact

As the HR Project Manager, you'll act as a trusted partner to the Chief People Officer, helping turn HR strategy into execution. Sitting at the center of the HR function, you'll bring structure, visibility and purpose to the initiatives that shape how we operate, scale and support the business.

Become the conductor of the HR roadmap , translating strategy into actionable plans, create structure ensuring the right priorities receive the right level of attention, and keeping critical initiatives moving forward.

Act as a strategic partner to the CHRO , providing visibility on priorities, risks, dependencies, budgets and delivery status across the HR function.

Own and elevate our HR project management methodology , continuously improving the way we plan, govern, track and deliver projects, care about details while embedding a culture of accountability and operational excellence.

Own the HR budget framework , maintaining a clear view of spend, commitments and personnel costs, and helping HR leadership make informed decisions through reliable data and forecasting; drive consensus about competing priorities and build trusted relationships across different departments.

Lead high-impact and strategic projects , from HR technology deployments and process redesign to cross-functional initiatives that improve the employee experience and support EPI's growth; prepare the organization for process and system change, delivery communications and training plans and support the adoption of new ways of working.

Drive innovation within HR , exploring how AI can simplify processes, improve decision-making and help us work smarter.

This role offers a unique opportunity to combine strategy, project management, operational excellence, innovation and business partnering while having a direct impact on how HR and the wider company evolve.

HR Technology stack

Pigment, to be rolled out in 2027

You’ll also work with Outlook, Slack, Confluence, SharePoint, OneDrive , and the Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

You’ll work on Mac

To succeed, you should meet at least 70% of these requirements

Mandatory company must-have

Fluent in English (CEFR C1 or C2); French, German, Dutch, or other European languages are a plus

Thrive in a remote-first, multicultural environment

Job specific requirements

Solid project management experience , with a strong command of project management methodologies and practices.

Strong proficiency with Jira or a comparable project management tool , including dashboards, reporting and data quality.

Previous experience working within an HR environment , with a good understanding of HR processes and operations.

Experience with budget management and follow-up , ideally including personnel costs.

Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office , particularly Excel and PowerPoint.

A proactive and autonomous mindset , with the ability to prioritize, anticipate needs and keep multiple initiatives moving forward.

A collaborative, low-ego approach, with the ability to build trust and influence without relying on authority .

We’d also value experience in the following areas

PMO, Chief of Staff, HR Consultant or transversal coordination experience , bringing structure and oversight across multiple teams.

Experience implementing or rolling out HR tools and processes in a growing organization.

Experience working in a highly regulated environment , such as payments, financial services or fintech.

Experience with Pigment , particularly in implementation, administration or Product Owner-type responsibilities.

Recruitment Steps Are

We Aim To Keep Our Recruitment Process Simple, Transparent And Efficient . You’ll Know What To Expect At Every Step

First conversation with François, Senior Manager, Talent Acquisition | 45 min

We’ll discuss your experience, your understanding of the role and EPI, and answer your questions. François will also make sure you know what to expect and help you prepare for the next steps.

Interview with Guillaume, Chief People Officer | 60 min

Guillaume will take you deeper into the scope and challenges of the role. You’ll discuss your HR background, project management experience and how you would approach some of the priorities ahead.

Interview with Gwenaële, Director, People Operations | 60 min

A final conversation focused on how you work: collaboration, prioritization, stakeholder management and navigating competing demands. This step may also include a practical business case to explore how you approach real-life situations.

Hopefully, an offer you can’t refuse

And of course,

each conversation goes both ways : you’ll have plenty of opportunities to ask questions, meet your future colleagues and decide whether EPI is the right next step for you.

Turn back if …

You need someone else to define your priorities and next steps.

We’re looking for someone who spots what needs attention, makes pragmatic trade-offs and keeps things moving.

You’re more interested in owning the spotlight than enabling others.

This role is about influencing without ego, building trust and helping HR experts deliver at their best.

You believe every project deserves the same level of attention.

You’ll need to stay calm when things get busy, distinguish critical from nice-to-have and balance ambition with the team’s actual capacity.

What we can offer

Remote-first culture

with quarterly and annual all-staff in-person meetups to keep teams connected and collaborative

Possibility to work from another EU country for up to 3 months per year

Competitive compensation package, featuring salary, performance-based bonus, and a thoughtfully designed, high-quality benefits program

The opportunity to be part of a multicultural European company

Learning & development budget : €5,000 training budget per year

Our commitment to equal employment opportunities

EPI offers the same job opportunities to all, without distinction of gender, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, social status, disability or age. EPI promotes the development of an inclusive work environment that mirrors the diversity of the clients our product is serving.
